name: Free Online Excel Formula Helper - ATools
description: Library of common Excel formulas with syntax, examples, and a simple interactive picker.
seoDescription: Free online Excel formula helper with a curated library of common functions such as SUM, IF, VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH. Each entry includes syntax, a short explanation and a practical example so you can build formulas faster without digging through documentation. Runs entirely in your browser with zero uploads, ideal for privacy‑sensitive spreadsheets and everyday productivity.

ui.title: Excel Formula Helper
ui.noSelection: Select a formula on the left to view details.
ui.noResults: No formulas matched your query. Try another keyword.
ui.formulaSumExample: Example: =SUM(B2:B10) calculates the total sum from B2 to B10.
ui.formulaAvgDesc: Returns the average (arithmetic mean) of numbers.
ui.formulaAvgExample: Example: =AVERAGE(C2:C100) calculates the average grade score.
ui.formulaIfDesc: Returns different results based on a condition for simple branching logic.
ui.formulaIfExample: Example: =IF(D2>=60, "Pass", "Fail") checks if the score passes.
ui.formulaCountifDesc: Counts the number of cells that meet a single condition.
ui.formulaSumifDesc: Sums cells that meet a specified condition.
ui.formulaSumifExample: Example: =SUMIF(B2:B100, "Marketing", C2:C100) sums sales by department.
ui.formulaVlookupDesc: Looks up a value in the first column and returns a value from the specified column.
ui.formulaVlookupExample: Example: =VLOOKUP(E2, A2:C100, 3, FALSE) looks up an employee's name by ID.
ui.formulaIndexMatchDesc: Combines INDEX and MATCH for flexible lookups; more robust than VLOOKUP with support for left-lookups.
ui.formulaIndexMatchExample: Example: =INDEX(C2:C100, MATCH(E2, A2:A100, 0)) looks up by ID in column A and returns column C.
ui.formulaTextDesc: Converts a number to formatted text (often used for dates or currencies).
